chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'I presented to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) the daughter of Hamza, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not know that she is the daughter of my brother from breast-feeding?'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad decline to marry the daughter of Hamza?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the legal principle that breast-feeding (radāʿ) creates a permanent marital prohibition akin to blood lineage, a key concept in Shia fiqh. Imam Ali’s proposal to the Prophet underscores the practical application of this rule within the Prophet’s own household, specifically regarding Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was breast-fed by Hamza’s wet-nurse. The hadith serves as a primary evidence for the extent of kinship established through wet-nursing in Islamic marriage law.
